raw_segments.text: Cleopatra. O Charmian, where thinks d' thou he is now? Stands he, or sits he? Or does
he walk, or is he on his horse? O happy horse, to bear the weight of Antony. Do bravely horse,
for what's d' thou whom thou mobst? The demi-atlas of this earth, the arm and bergannet of men.
He's speaking now, or murmuring, where's my serpent of old Nile? For so he calls me.
Now I feed myself with most delicious poison. Think on me that I am with phobus amorous
pinches black, and wrinkled deep in time.
Broad-fronted Caesar, when thou wast here above the ground, I was a morsel for a monarch.
And great Pompey would stand and make his eyes grow in my brow. There would he anchor his aspect,
and die with looking on his life.
